implementation_notes: The default C++ realization: a plain aggregate whose members are the former parameters, passed as `const DrawParams&`; brace initialization rejects narrowing conversions, and `= default` on `operator==`/`operator<=>` supplies the value semantics the language does not generate automatically. Use it while the group has no invariants; switch to a class with a validating constructor once construction must never produce an invalid carrier.
pitfalls: Brace initialization without field names is still positional: insert a member and every call site silently shifts, exactly like the parameter list it replaced.
Narrowing conversions are ill-formed inside braces ({2.0} for an int member), which is a feature but turns previously compiling calls into errors.
Passing the aggregate by value copies it; take `const&` unless the group is small and trivially copyable.

variants.name: Designated initializers (C++20)
variants.idiom_name: aggregate + designated initializer call sites (.field = value)
variants.implementation_notes: C++20 designated initializers give the aggregate named, order-independent construction (`.width = 1.0f`), the closest the language comes to keyword arguments; omitted members keep their default member initializers or are value-initialized. Use it where the toolchain is C++20 and call sites would otherwise repeat position-sensitive brace lists; the type itself stays an ordinary aggregate.
variants.code_sketch:
struct DrawParams { float x, y, width = 1.0f, height = 1.0f; };

drawEdge(DrawParams{ .x = 2.0f, .y = 3.0f, .height = 8.0f });
pitfalls: Designators must follow declaration order, so this is not a full keyword-argument replacement and reordering members breaks call sites.
Default member initializers make a class a non-aggregate in C++11 but are legal in C++14+, so the same declaration fails on older standards.
Mixing designated and positional initializers in one brace list is ill-formed; keep call sites uniform.

variants.name: Class with validating constructor (classic form)
variants.idiom_name: class with private members, validating constructor and accessors
variants.implementation_notes: When the group has invariants (order, non-empty, ranges), the classic class - private members, a constructor that validates and accessors - is still the right form, and it can carry group behaviour (contains, overlaps) instead of leaving that to call sites. Choose it over the aggregate as soon as construction must never produce an invalid carrier, or when member invariants must hold across the type's lifetime.
pitfalls: Accessors returning references to mutable members reopen the aliasing the constructor closed.
Without `= default` or hand-written comparison the class loses the equality an aggregate would have had cheaply.
A validating constructor tempts you to keep growing the class into a full value object; keep it a carrier unless the domain genuinely wants the behaviour.
